Multiplying by positive product prod(1+h lambda_i) yields degree <=m numerator with positive value at h=0; k positivity components require at least 2(k-1) positive root multiplicities, proving floor(m/2)+1 bound including tangencies. For arbitrary distinct roots t_j and distinct positive eigenvalues lambda_i, the proposed residue coefficients c_i make F(h) identically 2prod(1-h/t_j)/prod(1+h lambda_i) because poles and value at zero match. Set x=1,G=I,L=diag(lambda),r=Q=1,E_N(z)=1+c^T(z-1)+kappa||z-1||^2, kappa>||c||^2/4; this is everywhere strictly positive and strictly convex, with consistent auxiliary starting data. Independent exact sympy interpolation through m=6, and direct elimination for m=2 gave r+(h)=16(h-1)(h-2)/(609h^2+449h+32) with global minimum E_N=31/320>0.
